sources.title: Carta de Perigosidade de Incêndio Rural 2020-2030 (structural rural-fire hazard map)
sources.publisher: ICNF - Instituto da Conservação da Natureza e das Florestas, I.P. (published in Diário da República, Aviso n.º 6345/2022)
sources.license: Free open data with attribution (ICNF geoCATALOGO terms: "ICNF, <layer>, <URL>, <date>"); indicative only. Municipality boundaries: CAOP 2025, CC BY 4.0 (DGT).
sources.method: The official 25 m raster has five classes: 1 Muito Baixa, 2 Baixa, 3 Média, 4 Alta, 5 Muito Alta (15 = no data: urban land and water). The raster was laid over the CAOP 2025 municipality boundaries (pixel-centre rule). Rating = area-weighted mean class over the classified pixels of the municipality, rounded half up. The five classes are official; the mean-and-round step is an app-specific interpretation.
sources.notes: Mainland only (278 municipalities); Madeira and the Azores have no wildfire rating. The chart is a static 2020 baseline: later fires and land-cover change are not reflected. Averaging compresses the top of the scale: only 4 municipalities reach 5. In dense cities the rating only describes the small vegetated part of the municipality (Lisboa: 16% of the area is classified).

sources.title: Flood hazard maps of the 2nd-cycle flood risk management plans (PGRI 2022-2027): 100-year flood in the areas of significant flood risk (ARPSI)
sources.publisher: APA - Agência Portuguesa do Ambiente, I.P. (via SNIAmb and dados.gov.pt)
sources.license: No restrictions stated by APA (dados.gov.pt lists the licence as not specified; EU high-value dataset); attribute APA. Municipality boundaries: CAOP 2025, CC BY 4.0 (DGT).
sources.method: APA publishes hazard polygons only inside the 63 mainland ARPSI. The union of all 100-year (T=100) polygons was cut with the CAOP 2025 municipality boundaries, after removing permanent water (reservoirs, estuaries, coastal waters of the water-framework bodies) from both. Share = percent of the municipality's land inside the 100-year flood zone (overlaps under 1 ha ignored). Rating: 1 = no ARPSI flood zone in the municipality; 2 = under 1%; 3 = 1% to under 5%; 4 = 5% to under 15%; 5 = 15% or more. The thresholds are an app-specific interpretation; APA's own hazard classes are not used.
sources.notes: Mainland only (278 municipalities); Madeira and the Azores have no flood rating. Rating 1 means APA designated no significant flood-risk area there. It does not mean there is no flood hazard: ARPSI are mostly urban stretches chosen from past events and potential damage, so rural floodplains, small streams, flash floods and rain flooding in cities are not covered (Lisboa gets 2 although urban flooding is known there). The share also depends on the size of the municipality.

sources.title: NP EN 1998-1 (Eurocode 8), National Annex, Annex NA.I: municipalities with their seismic zone
sources.publisher: IPQ - Instituto Português da Qualidade (technical committee CT 115, coordinated by LNEC)
sources.license: The standard is copyright of IPQ and is sold by IPQ. Only facts are reused (the seismic zone of each municipality and the reference ground accelerations); no text of the standard is bundled.
sources.dataset_version: NP EN 1998-1:2010. The zone table was read from the CT 115 final-vote text of 2009-06-19 (https://www.oet.pt/downloads/eventos/EuroCodigo8.pdf) and checked against ACSS ET 05/2007 and a map of the published edition.
sources.method: The annex gives each municipality a Type 1 zone (1.1 to 1.6, distant large earthquakes) and a Type 2 zone (2.1 to 2.5, near moderate earthquakes), each with a reference peak ground acceleration agR in m/s2 (Type 1: 2.5, 2.0, 1.5, 1.0, 0.6, 0.35; Type 2: 2.5, 2.0, 1.7, 1.1, 0.8). Madeira has Type 1 only and the Azores Type 2 only. The governing value is the larger of the agR values the annex defines for the municipality. Rating: agR 2.5 or more = 5; 2.0 or more = 4; 1.5 or more = 3; 1.0 or more = 2; below 1.0 = 1. The zones are official; the rating bands are an app-specific interpretation. Óbidos was corrected from Type 1 zone 1.5 to 1.4 (confirmed by the two other sources); its rating is the same either way.
sources.notes: All 308 municipalities. agR is the design ground acceleration on rock for a 475-year return period. It ignores soil amplification, liquefaction, tsunami and local geology, and is one value per municipality. Taking the larger of two actions with different spectral shapes is a simplification. The published 2010 edition and the amendment A1:2013 could not be read directly. A new national annex for EN 1998-1-1:2024 may replace these values.

sources.title: European Landslide Susceptibility Map ELSUS v2, aggregated to Portuguese municipalities
sources.publisher: European Commission JRC, European Soil Data Centre (ESDAC); Wilde et al. (2018), Journal of Maps
sources.license: ELSUS v2 grid: CC BY 4.0 (open deposit of Wilde et al. 2018, doi:10.6084/m9.figshare.5878264). Municipality boundaries: CAOP 2025, CC BY 4.0 (DGT). Attribution required for both.
sources.dataset_version: ELSUS v2 (2018; open deposit version 3 of 2019-04-02), CAOP 2025 boundaries
sources.method: ELSUS v2 is a 200 m grid with five susceptibility classes: 1 very low, 2 low, 3 moderate, 4 moderate to high, 5 high to very high. Each cell is assigned to the municipality that contains its centre; no-data cells are dropped. Rating = area-weighted median class of the municipality (the smallest class where the cumulative share reaches 50%), read as the typical location. The five classes are the source's own; the median step is an app-specific interpretation.
sources.notes: This is EU-level data, not a Portuguese national product: no national landslide dataset (the issue named EROS/CCDR) was reachable as a static download. Mainland only (278 municipalities); ELSUS excludes Madeira and the Azores. It is a pan-European 200 m model made for scales of 1:200,000 or coarser, and its classes are relative inside each modelling region. The source rates its own reliability for these regions as good (9 municipalities), moderate (140), poor (71) or no information (58). Urban land lowers susceptibility (Porto gets 1). No municipality reaches 5, because the median hides steep minorities.
